Claim: Russian intelligence holds compromising sex tapes ("kompromat") of Trump from a 2013 stay at the Moscow Ritz-Carlton and can blackmail him (the "pee tape" allegation in the Steele dossier, sourced to unnamed Russian sub-sources).
Outlet: BuzzFeed News (published the full dossier); allegation from Christopher Steele's anonymous sub-source network
Reach: Very wide. BuzzFeed published the full 35-page dossier. FBI Director Comey briefed President-elect Trump on this specific allegation on Jan 6, 2017 (documented in the Mueller Report and the DOJ OIG report). The allegation was repeated for years across national TV, print and social media as the "pee tape".
On_Record_Denials_or_Contrary_Evidence: DOJ OIG FISA report (Dec 2019), https://web.archive.org/web/2020id_/https://www.justice.gov/storage/120919-examination.pdf: Steele's Primary Sub-source told the FBI the Ritz-Carlton allegation was "rumor and speculation" that he/she "had not been able to confirm"; the information came from "word of mouth and hearsay" and "conversation that [he/she] had with friends over beers", and the allegations about Trump's sexual activities were statements heard "in jest". Mueller Report Vol. II, https://cdn.cnn.com/cnn/2019/images/04/18/mueller-report-searchable.pdf: calls it "the Steele reporting's unverified allegation that the Russians had compromising tapes of the President". Trump has denied it (subject denial; not counted as proof).
Search_Performed_No_Evidence_Found: Full-text search of the DOJ OIG FISA report (Ritz, sexual, rumor and speculation, jest) and the Mueller Report (tapes, compromising). Neither reports any corroboration; OIG documents that the sub-source himself/herself disclaimed it. No tape or other evidence has been produced in any official record reviewed.
Corroboration_Found: None found. The Mueller Report notes an Oct 30, 2016 text to Cohen ("Stopped flow of tapes from Russia...") about rumored tapes; this shows the rumor circulated, not that tapes exist.
Notes: Overlaps catalog #10 (dossier claims generally); this row isolates the kompromat-tape allegation. Never call it a lie; it is unsupported.

Claim: Trump called Americans who died in war "losers" and "suckers" and skipped the 2018 Aisne-Marne cemetery visit for that reason.
Reach: Very wide (2020 and 2024 campaigns, national media).
On_Record_Denials_or_Contrary_Evidence: Denied at the time by Trump and several aides. However, former WH Chief of Staff John Kelly went on the record in October 2023 confirming the "suckers"/"losers" remarks (reported by CNN, NYT, NBC and others).
Corroboration_Found: YES: John Kelly (present as chief of staff) confirmed on the record, Oct 2023. The Atlantic URL loaded and was verified; Kelly's statement was seen only in secondary reporting (e.g., nytimes.com/2023/10/03/us/politics/john-kelly-trump-veterans.html; not loaded, 403).
Notes: Does not meet the Unsupported standard because a named person present corroborated it. The specific Aisne-Marne weather/rain detail is disputed, but the core claim is corroborated.

Claim: Russia paid Taliban-linked militants bounties to kill U.S. troops, and Trump was briefed and did nothing.
Outlet: The New York Times, anonymous officials
Claim_URL: https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/26/us/politics/russia-afghanistan-bounties.html (403 to our fetcher; URL and headline confirmed via search index; body text not loaded)
Reach: Very wide: Biden campaign attacks, congressional briefings, extensive national coverage.
On_Record_Denials_or_Contrary_Evidence: WH Press Secretary McEnany, June 29, 2020 (official transcript): "this was not briefed up to the President because it was not, in fact, verified" and "there is no consensus within the intelligence community", https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefings-statements/press-briefing-press-secretary-kayleigh-mcenany-062920/. DoD statement June 29, 2020 ("no corroborating evidence"; defense.gov release 2241964, which returned 403 to our fetcher, so its text was not verified).
Search_Performed_No_Evidence_Found: Biden White House background call, Apr 15, 2021 (UCSB): IC assesses "with low to moderate confidence, that Russian intelligence officers sought to encourage Taliban attacks against U.S. and coalition personnel ... including through financial incentives", https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/background-press-call-senior-administration-officials-russia
Corroboration_Found: PARTIAL: an IC judgment at low-to-moderate confidence supports the underlying bounty allegation. The "briefed and did nothing" element remains contested (denied on record by the WH; reported as being in a written PDB by anonymous sources).
Notes: Not Unsupported: some official intelligence support exists. Could be revisited as a narrower "Trump was briefed" item if a primary record emerges.

Claim: Trump knew in advance about the June 9, 2016 Trump Tower meeting (Cohen reportedly prepared to tell Mueller).
On_Record_Denials_or_Contrary_Evidence: Mueller Report Vol. I: "In an interview with the Senate Judiciary Committee, however, Trump Jr. stated that he did not inform his father about the [meeting]"; Trump tweet July 27, 2018 denial (quoted in the Mueller Report).
Search_Performed_No_Evidence_Found: Mueller Report searched for "told his father" and "did not inform".
Corroboration_Found: PARTIAL: Mueller Report: "Michael Cohen recalled being in Donald J. Trump's office on June 6 or 7 when Trump Jr. told his father that a meeting to obtain adverse information about Clinton was going forward." So an on-record (if disputed) account exists.
Notes: A named witness account exists (Cohen to the Special Counsel), so this is contested rather than unsubstantiated. Excluded.
